scenario: AITA for wanting my girlfriend to be less braggy about her work perks? She seems to forget that the way she lives isn't how most people live... | My girlfriend has a pretty sweet job. She doesn't have set hours; she just has to work 35 hours a week whenever is convenient for her and make it to her few meetings. She can work from the office or from home sometimes. She has a full benefits package despite being under what most people consider full time. A really nice retirement package too. And the company will pay everything for continued education. She does work she finds interesting (cutting edge robotics) and gets along well with her coworkers. She has a lot of PTO per year and her boss even lets the employees "earn up" more; if they work extra hours one week they can ask for the equivalent in PTO for later. Her team's managers buy them whatever they want for the office; they want a 500 dollar expresso maker, they get it. They want a type of fancy coffee, they get it. Nice furniture, done... They get paid well too; pretty middle of the road salary for robotics but she says the work life balance more than makes up for it. She'd rather have more time than be a top earner. And honestly a midrange robotics salary is still damn good. And anyway, For a while I thought "good for her" for having found something that she is happy with. But recently it's gotten frustrating because I think she forgets that this isn't how everyone lives. Like when we're out with my friends or just hanging out she'll talk about the nice stuff her managers bought for the office, about all the vacations she takes, about how she and her coworkers left the office in the middle of the day to see a movie then came back and just worked a little later. And yeah, it seems like she forgets that is no way a normal job. So last night we were at a party and she mentioned how she was going to tour a few new apartments Monday morning and afternoon, and one of the people at the party was like "don't you have work" and she said "yeah but I can set my own hours" And that just rubbed me the wrong way and I said that she needed to stop going on and on about her work perks, it was obnoxious and came off braggy. She was like "I was just explaining something" and I said it wasn't just this, it was everything. Most people don't live the life she lives." She said that I was coming off jealous and that it was a bad look. That she was where she was because she didn't settle for less; she studied and worked her ass off, and didn't let herself get too settled anywhere she was unfulfilled. And that instead of complaining, maybe I should ask myself what I'm feeling jealous of and what I need to do to get it. I told her she was missing the point; she'll always be around people who don't have what she does, and she could be a little more modest about it. She said I was the only one who seemed to have a problem with it, and stormed off... AITA for what I said?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this scenario is AITA (Ask if Truly Appropriate) for telling their girlfriend to be less braggy about her work perks. Let me break this down step by step. First, the girlfriend has a really great job with a lot of perks. She has flexible hours, can work from home, has a nice benefits package, good retirement plan, paid education, and a lot of PTO. She also gets to work on interesting projects and has a good work-life balance. It sounds like she's really happy with her job, which is awesome. But the issue is that she talks about these perks a lot, especially around friends and at parties. The person feels that she's bragging and forgets that not everyone has such a great job. The person mentioned that it's frustrating because she doesn't realize that her lifestyle isn't normal. They gave an example where she mentioned touring apartments during the workweek, and someone asked if she had work, to which she replied that she can set her own hours. The person felt this was obnoxious and told her to stop bragging. The girlfriend got defensive, saying she was just explaining and that the person was jealous. She also pointed out that she worked hard to get where she is and suggested the person should focus on their own goals instead of being jealous. Now, the question is whether the person was AITA for saying what they did. Let me think about this. On one hand, the person is feeling frustrated because their girlfriend is constantly talking about her job perks, which makes them uncomfortable. They feel that she's forgetting that not everyone has such a great job, and it's making them jealous or envious. It's understandable that they might feel this way because it's easy to feel left out or less accomplished when someone else is talking about their successes a lot. On the other hand, the girlfriend is proud of her achievements and is sharing them with others. She worked hard to get her job, and it's natural to want to talk about positive things in your life. She might not realize that her enthusiasm is coming off as bragging, especially if she's doing it in social settings where others might not have the same opportunities. So, is the person AITA? Well, it's a bit of a gray area. The person's feelings are valid, but the way they expressed it might have come off as accusatory or jealous, which could have made the girlfriend defensive. Instead of focusing on their own feelings, they might have made it about her behavior, which she took as criticism of her achievements. Maybe a better approach would have been to communicate their feelings without making it sound like they're criticizing her. For example, they could have said something like, "I feel a bit uncomfortable when we talk about our jobs because I know mine isn't as flexible, and it makes me feel like I'm not as lucky." That way, it's about their feelings rather than her behavior. However, the person did express their frustration, which is important. It's okay to set boundaries, but the way it's done matters. The girlfriend's response about jealousy suggests that she felt attacked, which might have been because the person's tone or words made it seem like they were upset with her rather than just expressing their own feelings. In conclusion, while the person's feelings are understandable, the way they expressed them might have been a bit harsh or accusatory, which could be seen as AITA. It's more about how they communicated their feelings rather than the feelings themselves being wrong.
